video_title: Jalen Duren and Pistons still have NO DEAL 😳 Will he stay in Detroit? 🤔 | NBA Today

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Duren and Pistons at an impasse regarding contract extension
quotes.excerpt: the Pistons and Jalen Duren are at an impasse and it's highly up in the air
quotes.quote: The Pistons and Jalen Duren are at an impasse and it's highly up in the air and questionable as to whether he will be reporting and showing up for media day in just seven days. Overall throughout this off-season both of these sides have been at an impasse where Jalen Duren, when he talked to people close to him, feels a certain way toward the Pistons' respect level for him. For him, it's been all about respect; for the team, it's been about business.

quotes.speaker: Tim McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim McMahon and Mark Jackson on the risks of Jalen Duren's contract situation
quotes.excerpt: if he ends up signing that qualifying offer, that is a disaster for Detroit

text_blocks.speaker: Tim McMahon
text_blocks.text: If he ends up signing that qualifying offer, that is a disaster for Detroit. You don't take a 180, 190 million dollar gamble to stay. If he signs the qualifying offer it's to leave, and that is a domino that could lead to some real big problems long-term in Detroit, which the whole reason they've taken this tough stance is because they're trying to keep this young core together.

text_blocks.speaker: Mark Jackson
text_blocks.text: I think the Sacramento Kings are wringing their hands like Birdman right now just kind of watching all this unfold. It's right now it's disastrous for the Pistons. This is a team that had the number one record in the East and now it's in flux and you're going into camp not happy and excited about what's next, you're going there with a black cloud.

quotes.speaker: Tim McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim McMahon on the negative impact of Jalen Duren playing on a qualifying offer
quotes.excerpt: you don't even really get him this year, you get a shell of himself
quotes.quote: He's not going to sit out. The worst case scenario is he signs the qualifying offer and he's playing for I believe it's 9.6 million dollars. And the problem then is you know he's looking to leave next summer and you don't even really get him this year, you get a shell of himself who is worried about making sure he's healthy and able to sign the contract that he wants somewhere else next summer. So you don't even get him fully on board this year.
